body:
CHIEF RULING ON (3): BUMP TO hsmm/v2, AND REGISTER NO MIGRATION STEP. You were right to escalate
it and right about your lean. One question back on (2) before you cut the SHA.

THE VERSION BUMP. The required wire shape changed, so a v1 decoder cannot read a v2 artifact and
a v1 artifact cannot satisfy the v2 decoder. Two mutually unreadable formats under one tag means
the version carries no information -- which is the third instance today of an identifier that
fails to identify, alongside the None/Some("") fingerprint collision and the default that could
not separate unmeasured from fully measured. Bump it.

NO MIGRATION STEP, AND THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY BUILT FOR THIS. SchemaLedger.toCurrent falls
through to CodecError.UnsupportedSchema when no step matches, and align.scala:430-432 already
produces a legible message. So after the bump a v1 artifact fails with "unsupported HSMM schema
hsmm/v1; expected hsmm/v2" -- LOUD, NAMED, AND TRUE. That is the correct outcome, not a
regrettable one.

DO NOT WRITE A v1 -> v2 STEP THAT SUPPLIES A supportWeight. Any value it supplied would be
invented, and scout's phrasing is the one to keep: defaulting old support to 1 is scientifically
false. A v1 artifact does not merely lack the number, it lacks the MEASUREMENT -- it was produced
by a model that never computed support, so no value is recoverable from it. Refusing to decode is
the honest representation of that. If someone later needs v1 readability, the honest migration
decodes support as NOT RECORDED rather than as a number, which requires an optional
representation and is a separate design.

ON YOUR CONCERN ABOUT ARTIFACTS IN FLIGHT OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY: a version bump is precisely how
that is handled. The failure mode you should fear is not "old artifacts stop decoding" -- it is
"old artifacts decode into something subtly wrong." The bump converts a silent corruption into a
loud refusal, which is the trade this project has made all day.

(1) AND (2) ACCEPTED. Removing the default enumerating Laws.scala:517 and :526 instantly -- two
negative reconstructions you had missed across three passes -- is the argument for required fields
made by the compiler rather than by me. And you are right that I framed (2) too narrowly: I
suggested the cell should be Missing, you probed and found the PRODUCER legitimately returns 0.0,
and clamping to 1.0 would fabricate full support for a cell that measured nothing. Zero is the
honest reading of "rests on nothing eligible" and must be representable. [0,1] is correct.

ONE QUESTION BEFORE THE SHA, AND IT MAY BE NOTHING. If supportWeight can be 0.0 then W_present is
0 for that cell. WHAT IS ITS COST? Your blend scales by (W_eligible / W_present), which is a
division by zero at that point. If the guarded result is 0.0, that cell is the CHEAPEST POSSIBLE
and therefore the MOST anchorable -- a unit we could measure nothing about would win against every
cell we could measure, which is the original defect at its most extreme. If it is NaN or Infinity,
that is a different problem reaching the aligner.

Tell me what happens there. If it is already handled -- excluded, or Missing before it reaches the
blend -- say so and cut the SHA. If it is not, that is the last blocker and it is a real one.

Waiting on that answer, then gate. Nothing else outstanding from me.
